chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Chicago 1919: the Deluxe Cabaret, Keppard, Bechet and Tony Jackson
summary: On tour in Chicago, Mazie Mullins took Briggs and Cook to the Deluxe Cabaret where he heard Freddie Keppard, Sidney Bechet and the pianist Tony Jackson.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And here's a wonderful thing that we should talk about this -- This was a group that was formed in London, an association that was formed in London in 1919. I want to show you this, this is the program. This was a culture group formed in London.

Okay, so now we've had a little interruption here while we're looking at a program which we're going to talk about in a little bit. Now, as far as the Southern Syncopators Orchestra, was that called the
Briggs
New York Syncopated Orchestra first, or was it called something else?
It was called the Southern Syncopated.
Southern Syncopated Orchestra.
That's the only name that I know of.
And so you were touring.
Yes, we were touring the United States.
And then you picked up Bechet in Chicago?
Chicago, yes.
Okay, tell me about that. That's interesting.

Well, we arrived in Chicago and our saxophonist Mazie Mullins, thought that she would take me out, being a kid, you know, to a cabaret, with Will Marion -- Dad Cook, and certain other members, to see,
Briggs

to listen to different bands playing in the City.

And we went to the Deluxe Cabaret

where --

I'm going to stop you there just a minute.

So, you went out and went to the Deluxe Cabaret?
Deluxe Cabaret, and we heard an excellent clarinetist, I didn't know who it was, but they seemed to know who it was. I was interested more in the trumpet player who was Freddie Keppard.
That was Keppard.
That was Freddie Keppard, yeh.

And we finally knew -- I finally knew that the clarinet player was Sidney Bechet. We say Bechet, but in France they say 'Bechette'.

The piano player was Tony Jackson.

You've probably heard of him, Tony Jackson?
Briggs
Yes, I have.
The other man I don't even remember, who he was. He was a string bass. If they had a trombone, I don't remember, but I'm sure it wasn't Kid Ory.
Right.
